Serpentis Regina Workroom: next-hour review

Proposed improvements · review only

October 30, 2026 · v0.8.0 · read-only review

Current hosted files were fetched through verified HTTPS and rendered locally in a fresh browser because the managed browser rejected the proxy certificate on direct navigation. All screenshots are new for this audit. Only invented fitting data was used; your own saved records were not accessed. Every screenshot below was visually inspected before acceptance.

Recommended hour

Keep the established visual style. Spend the hour making measurement context and comparison scope clear, reducing setup clutter and finding rows that need attention. Reserve a separate iteration for new sample fields and historical specification versions.

ChangeBudget
Visible Import workbook; collapse occasional sample setup and guidance10 min
Persistent sample/round/side/unit summary; explicit shared-target scope and revision guidance15 min
Filters with counts: Missing actual, Outside entered tolerance, Earlier definitions, Retained rows20 min
Check zero/null, switching sample/side, full CSV/PDF, phone/keyboard15 min

Technical-design gaps to address next

  1. Physical sample identity: unique sample label/ID, actual size, fit stage, measurement date, pattern revision and measuring conditions. Component sample records currently have name, round and notes; the separate Fit & comments fields do not create this binding.
  2. Measurement meaning: flat width versus circumference or panel width; seamline versus finished edge; relaxed versus stretched; before versus after wash. A +1 cm instruction needs this context. Preserve source methods and agree definitions rather than inferring conversions or allowances.
  3. Historical specifications: bind observations to the target/method version used for that fitting. Today target changes recompute comparisons for earlier sample actuals. Create a named revision before a fitting/specification change when you need a separate snapshot.
  4. Actionable fitting records: component/POM/sample/side → observed issue → agreed pattern/construction action → owner → next check. Being inside dimensional tolerance does not establish balance, drape, mobility or production approval.

Captured flow

1. Start

Usable, unclear first action

Tabs, labelled house-reference images and Save/Export are visible. Component import has no visible starting action; it is hidden until the file menu is opened.

2. Import

Clear after discovery

XLSX import is explicitly labelled, but sits inside a menu called Export. Put Import workbook on the main toolbar and label JSON download as a pack backup.

3. Set up a measurement

Correct concepts, crowded view

Component, sample/round, side and unit are explicit. The always-open new-sample form and guidance consume most of the available height. Collapse occasional setup controls once a sample is selected.

4. Compare measurements

Working calculations, important scope risk

After scrolling, the sample/round selector and target can leave view while actual/delta remain. Keep a compact active sample/side/unit summary visible. Targets/tolerances/proposals belong to the POM row and are shared across samples/sides. In this invented example, actual 20.5 stayed fixed while changing target 20 → 21 changed delta +0.5 → −0.5. This is comparison with the current working target, not a frozen historical specification.

5. Use a phone

Reachable actions, too much setup before rows

At 390×844 there is no horizontal document overflow and Save/Export stay visible. No POM row appears on the first screen. Collapse setup/guidance, wrap the active-sample summary and bring measurement rows closer to the top.

6. Prepare a fitting handoff

Useful fields, separate records

Fit & comments already has date/stage/size/pattern fields. They are not bound to the selected component sample. The next model should link physical-sample identity and measuring context to POM observations, then link issues to agreed actions, owners and rechecks. Tolerance compliance is not fit approval.

Accessibility and evidence limits

Small Ruby #E4002B labels on Electric #1E22AA have a calculated flat-color contrast of about 2.32:1. Matte ash #92989D on Obsidian #101820 is about 6.14:1. The fixed brand assignments are preserved in this review; a contrast-compliant treatment needs a separate brand decision. Size/spacing can improve legibility but do not by themselves fix an insufficient contrast ratio.

This is not a complete WCAG, screen-reader, keyboard or physical-iPhone audit. Phone findings use a 390×844 viewport. Capture and code inspection establish the stated behaviors; they do not test garment fit, manufacturing suitability or production approval.
